speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; to understand the underlying cause, could you please describe exactly where the pain is located and how long you have been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
You are a 17-year-old male with a 3-day history of left wrist pain, fever, chills, and malaise, following a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. You recently returned from a camping trip in Minnesota and are sexually active.

Given the constellation of fever, migratory joint pain (knee to wrist), and a history of outdoor exposure, I am concerned about Lyme disease or disseminated gonococcal infection. To differentiate these, please tell me: Do you have a rash, and if so, does it look like a bull's-eye or is it purulent?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, Blood Cultures, Gonorrhea/Chlamydia NAAT (urine and blood), and Lyme Serology.
REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide images of the skin lesions on your wrist and any other rashes you may have.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Temperature 37.7°C (99.9°F); Blood Pressure 120/80 mmHg; Heart Rate 80 bpm; Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Skin Examination: Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions noted on the dorsum of both wrists and hands; two lesions on the left palm. Musculoskeletal Examination: Left wrist shows swelling, erythema, and severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement. Complete Blood Count: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated); Hemoglobin 14 g/dL; Platelets 300,000 /μL. Joint Aspiration (Left Wrist): WBC >50,000 /μL (markedly elevated); Gram Stain positive for Gram-negative diplococci. Blood Cultures: Pending. STI Screen: Gonorrhea Positive, Chlamydia

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI).

The clinical picture of migratory polyarthralgia followed by an acute monoarthritis (left wrist), combined with fever and the specific finding of Gram-negative diplococci in the joint fluid, confirms this diagnosis. The characteristic painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists and hands are pathognomonic for DGI. You should be started on appropriate intravenous antibiotics immediately, such as ceftriaxone.
